value.rationale: Weak bridge coupling is a natural metastable transport problem. The global amplification peak grows to half the number of vertices, proving no dimension-free Wasserstein amplification bound even for symmetric irreducible path semigroups. The exact epsilon-log loss, order-epsilon constant, and peak-time constant quantify competition between fast within-well relaxation and slow interwell leakage; these precise spectral-geometric invariants are meaningful beyond qualitative mixing or computational correctness.
